players.product: retail colocation & interconnection (IBX data centers, Equinix Fabric) and xScale hyperscale data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 headline results (normalized, constant currency), per CFO Keith D. Taylor: 'Q4 revenues were $2,400,000,000, up 7% over the same quarter last year, fueled by continued strength in our monthly recurring revenues, which was up 10% over last year'; 'Global Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $1,200,000,000, or approximately 49% of revenues, up 15% over the same quarter last year'; a further line reads 'Global Q4 was $877,000,000 or up 13% over' the same quarter last year, including the seasonally higher recurring CapEx spend (the metric name is dropped in the transcript; the next sentence refers to 'Q4 AFFO'). CEO Adaire Fox-Martin: monthly recurring revenue 'grew 10% in Q4 and 8% for the full year'. Global Q4 MRR churn was 2.2%, lower than planned; full-year average quarterly MRR churn was 2.4%. The Q4 guide had assumed a large xScale Hampton lease that slipped into Q1, and Q4 carried one-time planned benefits that will not repeat in Q1; CFO: 'our fundamental underlying performance was meaningfully better than our expectations from top to bottom'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenues $2,400,000,000 (up 7%); MRR up 10% (8% for the full year); adjusted EBITDA $1,200,000,000 (approximately 49% of revenues, up 15%); $877,000,000 (up 13%, metric name dropped, AFFO context); MRR churn 2.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Record bookings and pre-sales: CEO said 'We delivered annualized gross bookings of $1,600,000,000 in 2025, up 27% year over year. Our Q4 bookings were $474,000,000, up 42% year over year and 20% from Q3, well ahead of our plan.' Q4 bookings 'were supported by an incremental pre-sales balance of $170,000,000, with more than $60,000,000 occurring in the quarter'. Into 2026: 'we have already booked approximately 45% of our Q1 2026 target, and signed an additional $100,000,000-plus of pre-sales as of today—already our largest pre-sales quarter ever.' Q4 transaction volume was 'the highest ever at over 4,500 deals with more than 3,400 unique customers'; 2025 had 'over 17,200 transactions, up 6% year over year with over 6,100 unique customers'. The team converted pipeline 'at around 49% in Q4'. CFO called Q4 'its best quarter ever by far', said retail delivered 'record bookings across each of our small, medium, and large size-of-deal categories', and said the 'backlog of cabinets sold but not yet installed stands at a record'.
quarterly_data.figure: annualized gross bookings $1,600,000,000 in 2025 (up 27%); Q4 bookings $474,000,000 (up 42% YoY, 20% from Q3); pre-sales balance $170,000,000 (more than $60,000,000 in Q4); approximately 45% of Q1 2026 target booked; $100,000,000-plus Q1 pre-sales; over 4,500 deals, more than 3,400 unique customers; pipeline conversion around 49%

quarterly_data.signal: AI share of demand rising: 'In Q4, approximately 60% of our largest deals were driven by AI workloads. That is up from approximately 50% earlier this year'. Of that AI 60%, 'nearly half of them were deployed by non-cloud and IT companies', i.e. by companies in the retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, financial services, and content sectors, which the CEO called increasing enterprise AI adoption outside the service provider community. She said the enterprise AI tailwind is emerging 'earlier, you know, as an enterprise footprint than we originally thought' when Equinix presented in the summer of 2025, and that growth in the AI service provider interconnection ecosystem is 'still early days'. Equinix positions itself for AI inference with 'network diversity, cloud proximity, AI-ready interconnection, and low latency'.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 60% of largest deals AI-driven (up from approximately 50%); nearly half of AI deals from non-cloud and IT companies

quarterly_data.signal: AI deals are denser and liquid cooling is spreading to enterprise customers: CEO said the AI deals showed 'a 33% increase in density compared to the non-AI deals, so an average of about 10 kVA per cab for these transactions', and 'we can certainly see that density increasing across our footprint'. 'We also had 11 liquid cool deployments in Q4, five of which were in our New York City facilities', supporting financial-services customers' use cases such as algorithm training. Customer example: Hudson River Trading selected Equinix because 'our global footprint and our advanced cooling solution enable them to achieve the latency and the density requirements' for next-gen AI trading workloads.
quarterly_data.figure: 33% increase in density vs non-AI deals; average of about 10 kVA per cab; 11 liquid cool deployments in Q4, five in New York City

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 guidance (point-in-time as of this call; normalized, constant currency): 'we expect total revenues to grow between 9–10%, which includes a modest 40 bps attributed to the NRR from the xScale lease timing'; MRR to grow between 8–10%; MRR churn comfortably within the targeted range of 2% to 2.5% per quarter; adjusted EBITDA margins approximately 51%, 'an expected 200 basis point improvement over 2025'; AFFO growth between 9–11%; AFFO per share growth between 8–10%, which after adjusting for 100 basis points of xScale lease timing is 300 basis points higher at midpoint than prior expectations from the past summer. '2026 CapEx is anticipated to range between $3,700,000,000 and $4,200,000,000, including about $280,000,000 of recurring CapEx spend', with no on-balance-sheet xScale spend included because those costs are expected to be reimbursed when the assets move into the xScale JVs. The quarterly cash dividend is to rise 10% per share, and total 2026 cash dividends paid will approximate $2,000,000,000. CFO declined to update 2027-and-beyond targets: 'it is a little premature to talk about 2027 and beyond'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue growth 9–10% (incl. 40 bps xScale NRR timing); MRR growth 8–10%; churn 2% to 2.5% per quarter; adjusted EBITDA margin approximately 51% (200 basis point improvement); AFFO growth 9–11%; AFFO per share growth 8–10%; 2026 CapEx $3,700,000,000 to $4,200,000,000 (about $280,000,000 recurring); 2026 cash dividends $2,000,000,000

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnection and cabinet metrics: 'Interconnection revenue grew 9% year over year'; 'We added 7,800 net interconnections in the quarter, including our adjustments'; Equinix passed '500,000 interconnections worldwide', which the CEO said is 'more than double our nearest competitor'. CFO: 'we added 4,300 net cabinets billing in the quarter, including cabinets from our MainOne portfolio', with underlying net cabinets billing up by 'the highest level in three years'; MRR per cabinet stepped up '$65 quarter over quarter', 'driven by very favorable pricing backdrops, increasing power densities, and strong interconnection attach rates'. CEO: 'very firm pricing throughout Q4 across all segments and for all regions'; the vast majority of contracts auto-renew with a pricing increment. On the clouds' cloud-to-cloud connectivity announcements, the CEO called cloud to cloud 'a simple connectivity use case' and said such announcements validate the network's role; Fabric provisioned VC capacity is 'stepping up quarter over quarter', with new developments to support MCP for AI agents and AI workloads.
quarterly_data.figure: interconnection revenue +9%; 7,800 net interconnections; 500,000 interconnections worldwide; 4,300 net cabinets billing; MRR per cabinet +$65 quarter over quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Named customer wins: 'Salesforce chose Equinix, Inc. to create a private multi-cloud networking layer for the engine inside their data and AI foundation. This is our largest global Fabric Cloud Router sale to date', deploying Equinix Fabric Cloud Router 'across 14 countries and 21 metros' to give private connectivity between Salesforce's presence in AWS, Azure, and other cloud service providers. Alimbic, an AI-powered marketing analytics platform, is deploying 'the NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Systems' with Equinix for distributed AI. BigMate uses Equinix Fabric to connect its edge devices, cloud providers and customer networks; Hudson River Trading selected Equinix for next-gen AI trading workloads; Honeywell expanded its relationship, including Fabric connectivity in Shanghai, Tokyo, and London, 'the first of many projects driving the integration of internal AI applications'. 'more than 60% of our existing customers added new services last year.'
quarterly_data.figure: largest global Fabric Cloud Router sale to date across 14 countries and 21 metros; more than 60% of existing customers added new services

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build and power: 2025 delivered 'record capacity', 23,250 cabinets in retail and 'more than 19 megawatts in our xScale business', with 'more than 30% of this retail capacity ahead of schedule'; Q4 delivered 'more than 12,000 cabinets to our retail business'. '52 major projects underway across 35 markets, including nine xScale projects'; 10 new expansion projects added since October and 16 major projects opened across 14 markets since the last call. Strategic land acquisitions in 2025 added 'approximately one gigawatt to our powered land under control balance'. CEO: 'we currently have three gigawatts of developable land under control', which is 'powered land, or land that we are close to securing the power on' - 'we are not in the business of, you know, surreptitiously buying a block of land if we are not sure that we can power that asset'. CFO: the 52 projects underway are 'energized projects' ('generally the retail space') in markets such as Chicago, New York, Dallas and Washington, citing one build of '67 megawatts'; in markets that are constrained 'not just for us but for the industry' Equinix demand-shapes customers to proximate metros. 'Capital expenditures were approximately $1,400,000,000, including our planned seasonally higher recurring CapEx of about $140,000,000.'
quarterly_data.figure: 23,250 cabinets and more than 19 megawatts xScale delivered in 2025; more than 12,000 cabinets in Q4; 52 major projects across 35 markets (nine xScale); approximately one gigawatt land added; three gigawatts developable land; Q4 capex approximately $1,400,000,000 (about $140,000,000 recurring)

quarterly_data.signal: xScale Hampton and JV: 'In January, we contributed our Hampton asset to the Americas JV, an important first step towards deploying $15,000,000,000 of capital across major metros in the U.S.' Hampton 'will support approximately 240 megawatts of IT capacity when fully built out'; 'The signing of the lease for half of this facility to a hyperscale customer is expected in Q1, and we expect the site to be fully leased later this year.' CFO: the Q4 guide had assumed a large xScale lease 'for two of the four buildings on the Hampton campus', now expected to close in the first quarter; the CEO said the shift 'simply reflects the fluid nature of xScale lease signings'. 'Of the approximate three gigawatts of capacity that can be developed, close to one gigawatt is currently earmarked for our xScale business', and xScale is expected to contribute to NRR over the next several years.
quarterly_data.figure: $15,000,000,000 Americas JV capital; approximately 240 megawatts Hampton IT capacity; lease for half the facility expected in Q1; close to one gigawatt of three gigawatts earmarked for xScale

quarterly_data.signal: Returns, cost and balance sheet: the 187 stabilized assets grew revenues 6% year over year, 'are collectively 82% utilized and generated a 27% cash-on-cash return on the gross PP&E invested'; CFO still sees stabilized assets growing '3% to 5%' as the typical range (Q4 was lifted by one-off price increases and higher density per cabinet). 'Revenues from owned assets are 70% of our recurring revenues.' Balance sheet approximately $40,000,000,000, with about $3,200,000,000 of cash and short-term investments; net leverage 3.8 times; issued $1,800,000,000 of senior notes 'at an effective rate of about 3.2%', with 2026 debt to be raised in lower-cost locations including Canada, Singapore, and Europe. SG&A is '18–19%' of revenue with a goal 'to get to 15% over some period of time'; CFO repeated the Analyst Day margin target of '52% plus'. CFO Keith D. Taylor has announced his retirement after 27 years and will stay as a special adviser over the next year; the successor search is 'well underway'.
quarterly_data.figure: 187 stabilized assets, revenues up 6%, 82% utilized, 27% cash-on-cash return; stabilized growth 3% to 5% typical; net leverage 3.8 times; $1,800,000,000 senior notes at about 3.2%; SG&A goal 15%
